summary: A constructor sets up a new object's fields. JavaScript allows one constructor per class, so default parameter values and static factory methods give you several ways to create an object.
notes: name = "New student" is used when the argument is missing or undefined. Passing null does not use the default.
A [] default is created again on every call, so it is not shared between objects like a Python default list.
static withScores(name, scores) is called on the class, Student.withScores(...), and returns a new Student.
pitfall: Writing a second constructor in the same class causes SyntaxError: A class may only have one constructor. Use default parameters or a static factory method instead.
contrast: JavaScript cannot overload constructors like Java, so it uses default parameter values like Python. It has no keyword arguments, so you pass undefined or write a static factory method to skip a parameter.
